skill.name: nosql-expert

content.value_statement: Distributed NoSQL schemas fail when teams model entities before access patterns. This skill guides query-first design for Cassandra, DynamoDB, and ScyllaDB.
actual_capabilities: Explains query-first modeling for distributed NoSQL systems.
Identifies hot partition risks and low-cardinality key choices.
Guides DynamoDB single-table design with partition and sort keys.
Summarizes Cassandra and ScyllaDB primary key design rules.
Provides a checklist for access patterns, cardinality, and consistency.
Highlights common anti-patterns such as scans, joins, and unbounded partitions.
limitations: Does not inspect a live database or cloud account.
Does not run benchmarks or capacity simulations.
Focuses on wide-column and key-value systems, not document databases.
Requires users to provide real access patterns and workload assumptions.

use_cases.title: Plan a New Service Schema
use_cases.description: Convert product access patterns into table and key designs before implementation.

use_cases.title: Review Production Hot Partitions
use_cases.description: Assess partition key choices and identify risks from skewed traffic or unbounded partitions.

use_cases.title: Compare Cassandra and DynamoDB Designs
use_cases.description: Evaluate design tradeoffs for consistency, indexes, denormalization, and query performance.

prompt_templates.title: List Access Patterns
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me list access patterns for a new service using DynamoDB or Cassandra. Ask for missing entities, query shapes, and scale assumptions.

prompt_templates.title: Design Table Keys
prompt_templates.prompt: Design partition keys and sort keys for these access patterns. Explain how each table or index serves one query efficiently.

prompt_templates.title: Find Partition Risks
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this NoSQL schema for hot partitions, low-cardinality keys, unbounded partitions, and consistency risks. Suggest practical fixes.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor a Relational Model
prompt_templates.prompt: Refactor this relational model into a query-first NoSQL design. Include denormalization choices, index strategy, and write consistency tradeoffs.

output_examples.input: Need a DynamoDB model for users, orders, and order history.
output: Access patterns are separated into profile lookup, user order history, and order detail lookup.
The design uses a user-centered partition for profile and recent orders.
The review flags order history growth and recommends time-bucketed partitions.

output_examples.input: Review a Cassandra table that uses status as the partition key.
output: The review identifies status as a low-cardinality key with hot partition risk.
It recommends a higher-cardinality key aligned to the main read path.
It notes that secondary indexes or filtering will not fix the core model issue.

output_examples.input: Compare Cassandra and DynamoDB for event lookup by device and time.
output: The response compares clustering columns, sort keys, and time-bucketed partitions.
It explains consistency and index tradeoffs for each platform.
It proposes validation questions for expected device volume and retention.

best_practices: Start with complete access patterns before choosing tables or indexes.
Choose partition keys with high cardinality and balanced traffic.
Document consistency requirements for each read and write path.
anti_patterns: Do not copy a relational schema directly into Cassandra or DynamoDB.
Do not use low-cardinality fields as primary partition keys.
Do not rely on scans, filtering, or joins for critical read paths.

faq.question: Does this skill write database code?
faq.answer: No. It provides design guidance, review criteria, and modeling patterns for NoSQL schemas.

faq.question: Which databases does it focus on?
faq.answer: It focuses on Cassandra, ScyllaDB, and DynamoDB, with emphasis on distributed key design.

faq.question: Can it help with MongoDB?
faq.answer: Only at a high level. The skill is not focused on document database modeling.

faq.question: Does it support production troubleshooting?
faq.answer: It can guide schema and partition review, but it does not inspect live metrics or run diagnostics.

faq.question: What information should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide entities, access patterns, expected traffic, data size, retention, and consistency needs.

faq.question: Is it safe for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: The reviewed skill is documentation-only and contains no executable commands or network behavior.
